definition: Security, legal, policy, runtime, capability and mandatory resource constraints that must pass before optimization or dispatch is considered.
A non-mutating, object-preserving semantic plan over current compute, router, WLU and allocator evidence. It is evidence for an execution route and is not admission or placement entitlement.
The mandatory fresh check of compute capability, router policy, WLU admission and Job-to-Node placement evidence immediately before mutation or dispatch.
A stable allocator-specific identifier for an execution node, distinct from provider resource identity or network endpoint.
Versioned capability evidence bound into placement and managed-target checks; stale or changed capability generations invalidate prior assumptions.
Health, freshness and runtime-state observations may influence preference and explanation but cannot grant admission, mint or release leases, or prove execution completion.
The Runtime Reference mechanism that binds an admitted and placed semantic operation to a local or remote implementation.

For LLM/model candidates, AI Model Router may select a policy-permitted route using authenticated WLU route evidence, but that plan is neither WLU admission nor executable/provider authority. GCI composes it as router evidence and still requires ordinary admission, allocation and handoff revalidation.
